title: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand
abstract: arXiv:2611.31083v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative AI has demonstrated human-level performance on technical work tasks, yet evidence on how these task-level capabilities are changing labor demand remains scarce. We study the firm-level adoption of GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms accounting for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. To identify causal effects, we exploit a natural experiment generated by firms' predetermined software procurement cycles. Early AI-adopting firms hired more workers before the launch of GitHub Copilot and had larger, more technical, and older workforces. After one year, GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effect on separations, overall technical headcount, or vacancy duration. translated_title: AI辅助编程与劳动力需求
translated_abstract: 生成式AI在技术性工作任务上已展现出人类水平的表现，然而关于这些任务层面的能力如何改变劳动力需求的证据仍然稀缺。我们研究了5,414家跨国公司对GitHub Copilot（一款AI编程助手）的企业级采用情况，这些公司占美国编程劳动力的38%。为了识别因果效应，我们利用了企业预先确定的软件采购周期所产生的自然实验。早期采用AI的企业在GitHub Copilot发布之前雇佣了更多员工，并且拥有规模更大、技术性更强、年龄更高的员工队伍。一年后，在因审查而采用的企业中，GitHub Copilot的采用使季度技术类招聘减少了29%，但对离职率、整体技术岗位人数或职位空缺持续时间没有影响。招聘放缓主要集中在涉及最高比例编码工作的初级技术岗位上。总体而言，AI编程辅助导致企业……
tldr: 该研究利用企业软件采购周期作为自然实验，发现采用GitHub Copilot后企业季度技术类招聘减少29%，且影响集中于编码工作量最大的初级技术岗位。
en_tdlr: Using firms' predetermined software procurement cycles as a natural experiment, this study finds that GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29%, with the effect concentrated in junior technical roles involving the highest share of coding work.
